description: This research report for the Iowa Department of Transportation, numbered 17-SPR0-013 and dated 2020, builds a system-level resilience framework that engineers can use to manage flood risk to the state's highway network. The researchers define resilience targets and functionality goals, characterise disruption scenarios across the network, estimate consequences as physical losses, traveller delays, economic impacts and loss of accessibility, and pick optimised mitigation measures in high-risk areas through case studies. Coverage is one US state at several levels of resolution. The Iowa Publications Online record offers two PDF files of about 5 MB and 1 MB, free to download; the licence is not stated and the abstract does not list results, which sit in the PDFs, which were not read. Caveats: the framework is customised to Iowa's network and flooding only, and models and data sources are not named on the record page. For simulation, it is a documented application of network resilience and hazard exposure analysis with climate adaptation relevance. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
